data.why: The app auto-loads its own bundled demo dataset (static/data/demo.json) on page load, fully exercising scarf plots, AOI metrics, and transition matrices with zero setup; a small synthetic CSV matching the app's generic 'Time,Participant,Stimulus,AOI,X,Y' upload format is also provided so the browser agent can exercise the upload workflow with a fresh dataset, including a missing-AOI fixation (off-stimulus gaze) and an out-of-bounds coordinate outlier.

goals: Load the bundled demo eye-tracking recording and read the resulting scarf plot to see how participants' gaze alternates between AOIs over time
Upload a new raw gaze/fixation export (CSV with Time/Participant/Stimulus/AOI columns) and confirm the app parses it into a dataset with the expected participants and stimuli
Build or inspect an AOI transition matrix to see which areas of interest participants look at in sequence
Add bar plots of AOI metrics (dwell time, fixation count, time to first fixation) and compare values across participants or stimuli
Export the computed metrics table as a CSV for further statistical analysis
Export a rendered plot (scarf plot or transition matrix) as a PNG/JPG figure

review.summary: The tree captures GazePlotter's purpose well: scarf plots, transitions, AOI metrics and CSV/PNG export. Labels are clean, and every screen I sampled supports its node. It should be filed after adding the time-binned AOI occupancy chart and workspace/Analysis saving (or listing them as not done), plus small fixes to t3, t10 and the f1/f2 notes.
